item.title: A Framework for AI-Ready Data in Earth and Environmental Science
item.description: arXiv:2611.27313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), specifically machine learning (ML), is increasingly integral to Earth and environmental research, yet the suitability of current research data infrastructures for supporting AI workflows remains poorly defined. While the FAIR principles provide a foundation for scientific data management, they do not explicitly address several requirements arising when datasets are used for training, evaluating, and deploying AI models. This article presents a practically motivated framework for assessing and improving AI-readiness of research data within distributed Earth and environmental data infrastructures. The framework was developed through a structured, community-driven process, beginning with a review of existing literature and readiness frameworks combined with feedback from a limited survey of scientists applying ML methods. Its main aspects were shaped by a multidisciplinary expert group representing data providers, infrastructure developers, data managers, and AI practitioners. It identifies 25 criteria covering data preparation, data quality, documentation, access, and supervised learning targets. The criteria emphasize aspects particularly relevant to AI applications, including provenance, treatment of missing data, bias documentation, uncertainty characterization, machine-actionable metadata, efficient access formats, and the quality and reproducibility of target generation. Application to a broad range of representative environmental use cases highlights how the relevance of individual criteria varies by application. We argue that AI-readiness should be understood primarily as a property of transparency and fitness for purpose rather than as a fixed level of data quality. The framework lays a foundation for communication and community-driven action to advance AI-ready data and support next-generation AI-enabled scientific workflows.

item.title: Pre-Crawl Prioritization and Seed Classification for Large-Scale Web Archiving
item.description: arXiv:2611.27743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pre-crawl prioritization systems decide which pages to fetch first before indexing, aiming to improve crawl efficiency and coverage. Existing approaches based on page popularity and relevance are unsuited to web-archival crawlers that prioritize comprehensive coverage over selective retrieval. We explore prioritization techniques tailored to web archival operations using URL lexical analysis, dynamic domain reputation systems, and HTTP response analysis to inform crawl scheduling decisions. By incorporating predictive models that estimate content change and disappearance probabilities, we improve crawl completeness while reducing redundant visits to stable resources. Through large-scale experiments, we demonstrate that our methods improve archival effectiveness and resource utilization compared to undirected crawling.
